strategy.summary: Reproduce the 32-bit-only NNLS divergence (gh-22791) by building scipy at the buggy commit d96ce7ab40f4 inside a genuine i686 environment, applying the developer's test_gh_22791_32bit, and running it. On the buggy revision the test should fail with coefficients around 1e15 to 1e16 failing assert_allclose; on the PR-fixed revision it should pass. A 64-bit host will not show the failure, so the i686 environment is the decisive requirement.

pip_packages: numpy<=2.2 (era ceiling; 2.2.4 is the reported version)
system_packages: i386 (32-bit x86) userspace or chroot, e.g. debootstrap --arch=i386 or an i386 Docker image
gcc 14.2.0 with -m32 support (gcc-multilib / i686 toolchain), gfortran for i386
libopenblas-pthread-dev for i386 (OpenBLAS 0.3.29, USE_64BITINT=0, NO_LAPACKE=1), detected via pkg-config
build_commands: git clone https://github.com/scipy/scipy && cd scipy && git checkout d96ce7ab40f4 && git submodule update --init --recursive
python3.13 -m venv /opt/venv32 && . /opt/venv32/bin/activate (run inside the i386 environment, so python reports a 32-bit pointer size)
pip install numpy==2.2.4 cython==3.0.12 pythran==0.17.0 pybind11==2.13.6 pytest hypothesis meson-python meson ninja
CFLAGS=-m32 CXXFLAGS=-m32 FFLAGS=-m32 LDFLAGS=-m32 pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
git apply the reproducing test diff onto d96ce7ab40f4 (adds test_gh_22791_32bit to scipy/optimize/tests/test_nnls.py)
pinned_because: numpy 2.2.4: era-inferred ceiling (numpy <= 2.2, newest at PR date 2025-04-05); numerically relevant, and the RandomState(42) draw order is part of the reproducer
scipy at d96ce7ab40f4 is the buggy source itself, not a pip release; no constraint is documented
cython 3.0.12: era ceiling <=3.0 and version reported in issue #22791; not numerically relevant

pythran 0.17.0 and pybind11 2.13.6: unbounded in the evidence (no documented constraint, no era table entry); chosen here as the versions reported in issue #22791 for reproducibility, not because a constraint was found
OpenBLAS 0.3.29 i386 pthread build: the reported numerical backend (32-bit, USE_64BITINT=0)

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/optimize/tests/test_nnls.py::TestNNLS::test_gh_22791_32bit (the class containing the existing test_2D_not_singleton_RHS_input_2 method)
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision d96ce7ab40f4 (run on i686), test_gh_22791_32bit FAILS because assert_allclose(coef, desired) sees coefficients of order 1e15 to 1e16 where desired has 1.05617285 and 0.23123048 etc. On the fixed revision (the PR #22802 head, with the spacing-based independence test in __nnls.c), the same test PASSES. The transition is the whole criterion.

input_output_examples.input: rng = np.random.RandomState(42); n_samples, n_features = 5, 12; X = rng.randn(n_samples, n_features); X[:2, :] = 0; y = rng.randn(n_samples); coef = nnls(X, y)[0]

risks: Architecture gate: the defect exists only on 32-bit (i686) builds or hardware. On an x86_64 host the buggy and fixed revisions both produce the correct answer, so the test passes on buggy and the transition does not occur. A 32-bit userspace or chroot, or qemu-i386 emulation, is required; without it this plan cannot produce the transition.
Toolchain and Python availability: a Python 3.13 i386 build and an i386 OpenBLAS 0.3.29 with USE_64BITINT=0 must be available; mixing 64-bit numpy with 32-bit scipy will fail to import or build.

Version inconsistency in the evidence: the issue body cites scipy 1.5.2 and 1.4.1, but the era ceiling is scipy 1.15 and the reported environment is SciPy 1.15.2. The 1.5.2/1.4.1 values are most likely typos or mislabeling. This plan relies on the era-inferred 1.15 ceiling and the buggy source commit, not on a documented constraint; no documented dependency constraint exists for any package.

The 1.4.1 reference values are from a different scipy generation; the test compares against them with default assert_allclose tolerance (rtol=1e-7), which is an era-independent choice in the test itself but is not documented as a numerical bound in the evidence.

Tolerance separation is not stated in the evidence; the failing buggy values (1e15 to 1e16) are so far from the expected values that the separation is wide in practice, but no exact threshold is known.
RNG dependence: the reproducer depends on RandomState(42) draw order (X then y). A different numpy RNG implementation would change X and y; numpy 2.2.4 is pinned for this reason.
Unrelated include: the stdio.h addition in the diff is a debugging artifact and not part of the numerical cause; it does not affect the transition.
Build time: building scipy from source for i686 can take a long time and needs a full Fortran and C toolchain, so the first build is expensive.

oracle.reference_source: issue #22791 expected coefficients, matching scipy 1.4.1 on 32-bit Debian
oracle.why: The test compares against known-good coefficients from the issue reporter's 32-bit run with the default assert_allclose tolerance; the 64-bit result is described as similar, so the same oracle applies there.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision on i686, nnls returns coefficients around 1e15 to 1e16 in place of the expected values (0.23, 1.06, 0.26 and zeros). assert_allclose raises AssertionError because the relative mismatch is enormous, which is the failure that distinguishes buggy from fixed.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision (PR #22802 head), the spacing-based independence test (fabs(pivot) > 100*spacing) avoids the cancellation on 32-bit, so nnls returns coefficients matching the expected values within default assert_allclose tolerance and the test passes.
